ety.text: From Middle English alredy (“fully; already”), equivalent to al- (“all, completely”) + ready. Cognate with West Frisian alreeds (“already”), Dutch alreeds (“already”), Afrikaans alreeds (“already”), Middle Low German alreide, alreids ("already"; whence modern German Low German alreeds (“already”)), Danish allerede (“already”), Swedish allaredan (“already”), Norwegian Nynorsk allereie (“already”). More at all, ready. The use as an intensifier in American English is a semantic loan from Yiddish שוין (shoyn), attested from 1903.

senses.d: Prior to some specified time, either past, present, or future; by this time; previously.
ex: I was surprised that she hadn’t already told me the news.
Much of what he said I knew already.

senses.d: An intensifier used to emphasize impatience or express exasperation.
ex: I wish they'd finish already, so we can get going.

senses.d: Indicates the completion of an action (whether past or hypothetical), or more generally, perfective aspect.
ex: You frame the picture for me already anot?
“Yah, I sign already,” my mother replied.

senses.d: Marks a change in state, more or less in the same manner as the inchoative aspect.
ex: I don’t think he can take it already.
Your ice cream is melting already.

grp.label: intensifier used to emphasize impatience or express exasperation

ety.text: From Middle French desia, from Old French des ja corresponding to dès + jà.
Inherited from Latin iam (“already, now”). Cognate with Portuguese já and Spanish ya.

es:ya.gl: now, right now, (in the negative) anymore, no longer

ety.text: Inherited from Old Spanish ya (“already; now”), from Latin iam. Compare Ladino ya, Asturian yá, Galician xa, Portuguese já, Catalan ja, French déjà, and Italian già.

pt:já.gl: already (indicating that something has happened before)

ety.text: From Old Galician-Portuguese ja, from Latin iam (“already”). Compare Spanish ya.
Univerbation of en + fin. Literally, “in the end”.

pt:de uma vez.gl: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see de, uma, vez.

phr: that train has already left the station
